title: fastpath: add safe-mode gating + deterministic fallback for precision/scheduler/KV cache
author: Priya Raman
description: Context: fast-path kernels and aggressive scheduler heuristics gave a ~20% p50 latency improvement but surfaced intermittent correctness deviations and KV-cache edge cases (especially for short prefix reuse and mixed precision fallbacks). This PR adds a conservative 'safe-mode' gate for the fast path, deterministic precision fallback paths, and KV-cache consistency checks. Goal: preserve most perf wins while ensuring correctness under corner inputs and enabling staged rollout. Changes include: 1) fastpath gating flag (runtime config + per-request header) that disables fast kernels when enabled; 2) precision toggle flow rewritten so kernel selection tries fp16 -> quantized-int8 -> deterministic-fp32 fallback with explicit checksum validation when crossing variants; 3) scheduler changes to reduce speculative batching for requests that hit new fallbacks (avoids interleaving KV cache writes); 4) KV cache safety checks and repair path that can replay a small suffix to rebuild consistent state; 5) telemetry counters and alerting hooks for fallback frequency, checksum failures, and batch aborts; 6) integration tests and a perf-canary harness to measure rollout impact. Rollout plan: feature-flagged, default off for enterprise customers currently using Dedicated; opt-in A/B via rollout config in Console; immediate enable in test clusters. Motivation: prior incident (SUP-1423) where a rare precision transition combined with an expired KV entry produced truncated outputs. This PR closes the correctness gap while giving operators control to prioritize performance vs absolute deterministic behaviour.

review_thread: Alex Chen (2026-02-11): Nice approach. Two asks: (1) ensure the checksum computation is cheap and can be skipped in non-debug builds; (2) can we make the per-request header opt-in rather than opt-out?

Priya Raman (2026-02-11): Replied: checksum uses a 64-bit xxhash and is gated behind a config flag; added microbench in kernel_selector to show <0.2% impact. Per-request header is opt-in (x-redwood-fastpath-safe-mode=true) — clarified in docs.
Marta Lopez (2026-02-12): Scheduler change looks risky for throughput. Can we add a conservative threshold so only sequences with >1 fallback in last N seconds throttle speculative batching?

Priya Raman (2026-02-12): Added adaptive threshold: speculative batching disabled when fallback_rate > 0.5% over sampling window or when request explicitly opts into safe-mode. Added unit tests for threshold logic.
Jordan Blake (2026-02-15): Please add a migration note for Dedicated customers; also add an emergency switch to force fastpath off cluster-wide.
Priya Raman (2026-02-16): Added cluster-wide emergency flag (runtime/flags.yaml) and dedicated deployment notes in docs/runtime/fastpath-safe-mode.md.
ci_checks: perf-regression: baseline +4% p50 on one canary shard (within accepted threshold)
release_notes: Adds a configurable 'safe-mode' for fast-path kernels which trades some latency for deterministic correctness. Includes deterministic precision fallbacks, KV-cache consistency checks, and telemetry for fallback events. Feature-flagged and rolled out gradually.
notes_for_ops: Default: safe-mode off. To enable cluster-wide safe-mode set runtime.flag.fastpath_safe_mode = true. Emergency kill-switch: runtime.flag.fastpath_enable = false. Watch metrics.redwood.fallback.count and metrics.redwood.kv.checksum_failure. If perf regression > 10% p50, rollback via Console rollout or set fastpath_enable=false.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover kernel selector, scheduler threshold, and kv repair logic. Integration tests simulate mixed-precision transitions, short-prefix KV reuse, and replay-based repair. Perf-canary run executed across 3 canary shards; observed median p50 regression of 3-7% depending on workload; rollout configured to ramp slowly.
release_strategy: feature-flagged rollout: start in test clusters -> opt-in in Dedicated for small subset -> automatic A/B for hosting (5% initial traffic) -> monitor fallback metrics -> ramp to 100% if stable. Emergency rollback via fastpath_enable flag.
